identification.name: Inconel 625 (Annealed)
identification.common_form_notes: Available as sheet (ASTM B443), plate (B443), bar/rod (B446), tube (B444), and welded pipe (B705) from aerospace and corrosion-resistant alloy suppliers. Supplied as gas-atomised powder (15–45 µm) for metal AM. Also used as weld filler wire (ERNiCrMo-3, AWS (American Welding Society) A5.14). UNS N06625, Werkstoff Nr. 2.4668, DIN (German industrial standard) NiCr22Mo9Nb.
identification.notes: Inconel 625 is a solid-solution-strengthened nickel–chromium–molybdenum–niobium superalloy (UNS (Unified Numbering System) N06625). Properties are for the annealed condition (980–1150°C, air cool) per ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials) B443/B446. Unlike Inconel 718, no precipitation hardening is required — Mo (8–10%) and Nb (3.2–4.2%) in solid solution provide strength up to ~982°C without a complex ageing cycle. Exceptional corrosion resistance: superior pitting, crevice, and intergranular corrosion resistance in seawater and aggressive chloride environments; resists both oxidising and reducing acids. Max continuous service temperature ~982°C (short-term oxidation resistance to 1093°C; mechanical strength is limiting above ~982°C). Cryogenic toughness is excellent — Charpy impact energy 47–66 J at −196°C, suitable for cryogenic tankage and LNG (liquefied natural gas) service. Weldability is outstanding: no post-weld heat treatment is required to maintain corrosion resistance (not susceptible to sensitisation), and 625 is widely used as weld overlay and cladding (filler wire ERNiCrMo-3). In metal AM (additive manufacturing) (DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering)/SLM (Selective Laser Melting)/LPBF (laser powder bed fusion)), 625 is one of the most printable superalloys — it does not suffer the hot cracking from γ″ precipitation that challenges Inconel 718 during AM. As-built SLM parts exhibit columnar dendritic microstructure with significantly higher strength (UTS (ultimate tensile strength) up to ~1,240 MPa) but reduced ductility compared with wrought annealed; solution anneal and HIP (Hot Isostatic Pressing) restore ductility and eliminate porosity. Hardness HV (Vickers hardness) 200 is approximate, converted from 190 HB (Brinell hardness). Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS/√3 = 930/√3 ≈ 537 MPa. Electrical conductivity derived from resistivity 1.29 µΩ·m: (0.01724/1.29) × 100 ≈ 1.3% IACS (International Annealed Copper Standard). Melting range: solidus 1290°C, liquidus 1350°C (MatWeb). Thermal diffusivity is derived from thermal conductivity (k), density (ρ), and specific heat (Cp) — not an independently measured value.

typical_usage: Seawater and offshore hardware (risers, subsea valves, umbilicals); chemical process vessels and piping; flue gas desulphurisation systems; aerospace engine components (combustor liners, exhaust systems) above 700°C; cryogenic tankage and LNG equipment; nuclear waste containment; weld cladding and hardfacing on lower-alloy substrates.
